# [BLO-15567](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-15567)

**Files:** `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`, `src/server/inherit-allowlist.ts`, `src/server/inherit-allowlist.test.ts`

Redirected `CARGO_HOME` and `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` onto the ephemeral cache root, alongside the seven cache paths already named there. **The two keys are here for different reasons and the PVC win belongs to `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` alone** (corrected after Ally review on [#2041](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2041); the original rationale claimed both were `$HOME`-derived, which is false for `CARGO_HOME`). `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is genuinely unset in the image, so it defaults to `<pkg>/target` **inside the checkout** — on the CephFS PVC under `workspace` isolation, where `homeRoot` is `/paperclip/instances/default/data/k8s-isolation/workspaces/<uuid>/home` with `storage.home: "persistent"`. That is the byte-moving fix. `CARGO_HOME` by contrast is image-set — `ENV CARGO_HOME=/home/node/.cargo` at `Dockerfile.agent-toolchain:327`, added 2026-08-30 in `a7d4db965` — and `/home/node` is the container overlay, never a mount, so on a pod running that image or newer the redirect moves an already-ephemeral cache. It is kept for two reasons that survive the correction: an explicit manifest env is independent of image-**rollout** state, so it also covers pods still on an image older than `a7d4db965`; and it bounds the cache under the volume `sizeLimit` rather than node ephemeral-storage. Not hypothetical — re-measured 2026-09-26: the 1.75 GiB of `.cargo` is concentrated in **8** isolation workspace homes, and **5 carry real registry writes (`registry/src/**`, `.cargo-ok`) dated 2026-09-03 → 09-10**, i.e. after the image ENV landed. Whether that is rollout lag or the non-claude `opencode_k8s` path (BLO-15567 AC3, gated on [BLO-15643](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-15643)) is **not established** and is recorded as an observation, not a diagnosis. Those bytes are pre-existing either way: **this change does not reclaim them**, and a separate reclaim pass is still required. ⚠ Tradeoff accepted: `target/` now lands on the `runtime-cache` emptyDir, which carries `RUNTIME_CACHE_SIZE_LIMIT` (20Gi) shared with eight other caches including Playwright browsers — exceeding an emptyDir `sizeLimit` evicts the pod mid-run, abrupt where PVC overflow was slow and visible. Low probability at current Rust volume; revisit if it grows. **`RUSTUP_HOME` is deliberately excluded and a test pins its absence** — the image installs the toolchains into `/usr/local/rustup`, so pointing it at an empty ephemeral dir would remove every toolchain and break `cargo`/`rustc` fleet-wide; `CARGO_HOME` is safe by contrast, verified empty in the image with `cargo` on PATH at `/usr/local/bin`, so it only accumulates a regenerable registry cache. Verified with a real `cargo build` **with CWD on the PVC** (the control that matters — see below) under both redirects and an untouched `RUSTUP_HOME`: compiles, output lands off `/paperclip`, no local `target/` created. **pnpm is deliberately NOT handled here, and the doc comment says so.** The first draft of this change also set `PNPM_HOME`, on a test run with CWD on `/runtime-cache` — same device as the target — where the redirect appears to work. It does not: pnpm hardlinks store objects into `node_modules`, so with a checkout on the PVC it silently ignores any cross-device store path and falls back to `<mount>/.pnpm-store`. Re-measured with CWD on `/paperclip`, both `PNPM_HOME=/runtime-cache/...` and `XDG_DATA_HOME=/runtime-cache/...` resolve to `/paperclip/.pnpm-store/v11`. That half is [#2036](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2036) / [BLO-36583](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-36583), which points `PNPM_HOME` at a **shared same-device** path instead — the correct fix, and the two changes do not overlap. Both spreads here are mutation-tested: reverting either one **alone** reddens the suite (isolated branch → the `workspace`-mode test, which also asserts no value starts with `/paperclip`; `RUNTIME_CACHE_ENV` → the default-cache test), per the CEO ruling on [BLO-34263](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-34263) that a guard with no failing mutation is documentation. The two names are also declared `SAFE_LITERAL` in `ENV_NAME_CLASSIFICATION` (the BLO-29804 gate caught their absence fail-closed) and added to the toolchain-cache block of the inherit allowlist, for the reason that block already states.
